verdicts.note: End-of-life care preferences among Chinese adults.
Book review of Chiappori on matching and marriage. C.7.a's.

Value transmission versus modelling in the parental home as explanations of adolescents' EXPECTATIONS about the timing of LEAVING HOME and later family events. Intergenerational transmission of the schedule itself -- A.19's mechanism operating on A.23's exposure.
Diversifying family structures for US adolescents, with co-residence with grandparents among the trends described. The adolescent is the child, not the pre-launch adult.
Parental status and custodial arrangements in repartnering.
Caregiving and care sharing across the life course.
No abstract; decline in US child physical abuse.
Gated decoy. Trends in US children living in SHARED HOUSEHOLDS, SIPP and ACS. The arrangement measured from the child's side; exposure trend.
EEG study of morphological parsing; 'family size' is the lexical statistic.
Age-period-cohort analysis of ATTITUDES toward parent-child co-residence in later life.

PARENTAL CORESIDENCE in young adulthood against psychological wellbeing, Add Health, with role, economic and health changes as mediators. The pre-launch exposure with a wellbeing outcome; the mediator set is close to §9's.
China's elderly care policy framework.
Stepfamily structure and intergenerational transfers in the PSID, noting that earlier data covered only CORESIDENT stepkin. Transfers as outcome.
Ethnography of Roma women's reproductive lives across Romania and Spain.
Intergenerational relationships of Vietnamese aged 60+.
No abstract; historical roots of European social capital in family structure. D.1.b-adjacent.
Grandparental care across Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam. C.2.a's exposure.

Comparative East Asian Social Survey modules on family attitudes and formation, Korea, Taiwan and China 2006-2016. Attitude and behaviour trends in the extended arm's region with a harmonised instrument.
Thesis on marriage and fertility determinants in China and Japan; whether the living arrangement is among the determinants is not visible.
Pregnancy after stillbirth, phenomenological study.
Long-term care workforce and intergenerational learning.
Whether parental and GRANDPARENTAL supervision time are substitutes or complements. C.2.a's, with a child outcome.
Remarriage and stepfamilies in early modern Spain.
Household size and CO-RESIDENCE across 12 Asian countries 1980-2010, household and individual perspectives. Companion to the 13-country record in batch 19; keep one at assembly.
Norms, perceptions and aspirations against Chinese demographic patterns. D.1.a's.
Family law festschrift chapter.
Essays on gender, migration and development.
Index of a volume on childlessness.
Untitled dataset record for the leaving-home-and-diet study.
No abstract; adolescent transition health care.
Second untitled dataset record for the same diet study.
No abstract; 'Conceiving Parents', legal.
Biographical chapter on A. E. Housman's childhood.
Attachment disorganisation and maladaptation.
Profile of members of a communal religious sect.
No abstract; postnatal follow-up expectations in a French maternity unit.
Fertility desires and pregnancy incidence by HIV status in Rakai.
No abstract; gated decoy. Co-residence with mother-in-law and maternal ANAEMIA in rural India -- the arrangement as exposure with a health outcome.
No abstract; transition care in Turner syndrome.
Reconstruction of PATRILOCAL, MATRILOCAL and intermediate marriage location among nineteenth-century Ukrainian peasant families. Historical variation in the residence rule itself.

No abstract; intergenerational space and intimacy during partnering and early parenthood among Tongan-Australian families. Close to the mechanism §1 names -- privacy -- but no fertility outcome visible.
Fatherhood after separation and its spatial organisation.
REGISTER-based study of economic difficulties during the transition to adulthood in Finland. Register measurement of the transition; C.5.a owns the exposure.

Timing of LEAVING THE PARENTAL HOME, first marriage and FIRST PARENTHOOD compared across CHINA, GERMANY and the USA for cohorts born 1933-1988, using large panel studies. All three events, three countries spanning both arms' regimes, and cohort depth -- the best comparative record in the frame for placing the two configurations side by side.
No abstract; active travel and the built environment in China.
Essay on pregnancy in surgical training.
No abstract; marriage market dynamics and the age gap. C.7.a's.

Parents' socioeconomic position against children's transition to FIRST UNION AND PARENTHOOD, UK Household Longitudinal Study, n=35,880. Large panel with both downstream links; the arrangement is not the exposure but the data would support it.
Evolutionary view of menopause.
Parental knowledge about childhood fever.
Depression among Iranian schoolgirls.

Japanese students' attitudes to the IE ideology -- the traditional household in which the wife cares for her husband's parents in ONE HOUSEHOLD. The norm that produces the extended configuration, measured as an attitude. D.2.b's, but directly upstream of this chapter's exposure in Japan.
No abstract; second-child fertility intentions among urban working women in Hunan. Chinese second-child intention studies frequently carry co-residence and grandparental care as regressors; trace.
Demographic transition and social network differentiation.

'Becoming Independent: LEAVING HOME, Cohabitation, Marriage, and PARENTHOOD' -- the chapter takes the whole chain as its subject and notes that young adults increasingly live independently BEFORE marriage, which decouples the arrangement from the union. That decoupling is what makes A.23 separable from A.7 at all.
